dwa.name: max_vel_trans
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the maximum translational velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: min_vel_trans
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the minimum translational velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: max_vel_x
dwa.desc: The maximum x velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: min_vel_x
dwa.desc: The minimum x velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: max_vel_y
dwa.desc: The maximum y velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: min_vel_y
dwa.desc: The minimum y velocity for the robot in m/s

dwa.name: max_vel_theta
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the maximum rotational velocity for the robot in rad/s

dwa.name: min_vel_theta
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the minimum rotational velocity for the robot in rad/s

dwa.name: acc_lim_x
dwa.desc: The acceleration limit of the robot in the x direction

dwa.name: acc_lim_y
dwa.desc: The acceleration limit of the robot in the y direction

dwa.name: acc_lim_theta
dwa.desc: The acceleration limit of the robot in the theta direction

dwa.name: acc_lim_trans
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the maximum translational acceleration for the robot in m/s^2

dwa.name: prune_plan
dwa.desc: Start following closest point of global plan, not first point (if different).

dwa.name: xy_goal_tolerance
dwa.desc: Within what maximum distance we consider the robot to be in goal

dwa.name: yaw_goal_tolerance
dwa.desc: Within what maximum angle difference we consider the robot to face goal direction

dwa.name: trans_stopped_vel
dwa.desc: Below what maximum velocity we consider the robot to be stopped in translation

dwa.name: theta_stopped_vel
dwa.desc: Below what maximum rotation velocity we consider the robot to be stopped in rotation

dwa.name: sim_time
dwa.desc: The amount of time to roll trajectories out for in seconds

dwa.name: sim_granularity
dwa.desc: The granularity with which to check for collisions along each trajectory in meters

dwa.name: angular_sim_granularity
dwa.desc: The granularity with which to check for collisions for rotations in radians

dwa.name: path_distance_bias
dwa.desc: The weight for the path distance part of the cost function

dwa.name: goal_distance_bias
dwa.desc: The weight for the goal distance part of the cost function

dwa.name: occdist_scale
dwa.desc: The weight for the obstacle distance part of the cost function

dwa.name: twirling_scale
dwa.desc: The weight for penalizing any changes in robot heading

dwa.name: stop_time_buffer
dwa.desc: The amount of time that the robot must stop before a collision in order for a trajectory to be considered valid in seconds

dwa.name: oscillation_reset_dist
dwa.desc: The distance the robot must travel before oscillation flags are reset, in meters

dwa.name: oscillation_reset_angle
dwa.desc: The angle the robot must turn before oscillation flags are reset, in radians

dwa.name: forward_point_distance
dwa.desc: The distance from the center point of the robot to place an additional scoring point, in meters

dwa.name: scaling_speed
dwa.desc: The absolute value of the velocity at which to start scaling the robot's footprint, in m/s

dwa.name: max_scaling_factor
dwa.desc: The maximum factor to scale the robot's footprint by

dwa.name: vx_samples
dwa.desc: The number of samples to use when exploring the x velocity space

dwa.name: vy_samples
dwa.desc: The number of samples to use when exploring the y velocity space

dwa.name: vth_samples
dwa.desc: The number of samples to use when exploring the theta velocity space

dwa.name: use_dwa
dwa.desc: Use dynamic window approach to constrain sampling velocities to small window.

dwa.name: restore_defaults
dwa.desc: Restore to the original configuration.

teb.name: teb_autosize
teb.desc: Enable the automatic resizing of the trajectory during optimization (based on the temporal resolution of the trajectory, recommended)

teb.name: dt_ref
teb.desc: Temporal resolution of the planned trajectory (usually it is set to the magnitude of the 1/control_rate)

teb.name: dt_hysteresis
teb.desc: Hysteresis that is utilized for automatic resizing depending on the current temporal resolution (dt): usually 10% of dt_ref

teb.name: global_plan_overwrite_orientation
teb.desc: Some global planners are not considering the orientation at local subgoals between start and global goal, therefore determine it automatically

teb.name: allow_init_with_backwards_motion
teb.desc: If true, the underlying trajectories might be initialized with backwards motions in case the goal is behind the start within the local costmap (this is only recommended if the robot is equipped with rear sensors)

teb.name: max_global_plan_lookahead_dist
teb.desc: Specify maximum length (cumulative Euclidean distances) of the subset of the global plan taken into account for optimization [if 0 or negative: disabled; the length is also bounded by the local costmap size]

teb.name: force_reinit_new_goal_dist
teb.desc: Force the planner to reinitialize the trajectory if a previous goal is updated with a seperation of more than the specified value in meters (skip hot-starting)

teb.name: force_reinit_new_goal_angular
teb.desc: Force the planner to reinitialize the trajectory if a previous goal is updated with a rotational difference of more than the specified value in radians (skip hot-starting)

teb.name: feasibility_check_no_poses
teb.desc: Specify up to which pose on the predicted plan the feasibility should be checked each sampling interval

teb.name: exact_arc_length
teb.desc: If true, the planner uses the exact arc length in velocity, acceleration and turning rate computations [-> increased cpu time], otherwise the euclidean approximation is used.

teb.name: publish_feedback
teb.desc: Publish planner feedback containing the full trajectory and a list of active obstacles (should be enabled only for evaluation or debugging purposes)

teb.name: visualize_with_time_as_z_axis_scale
teb.desc: If this value is bigger than 0, the trajectory and obstacles are visualized in 3d using the time as the z-axis scaled by this value. Most useful for dynamic obstacles.

teb.name: global_plan_viapoint_sep
teb.desc: Min. separation between each two consecutive via-points extracted from the global plan [if negative: disabled]

teb.name: via_points_ordered
teb.desc: If true, the planner adheres to the order of via-points in the storage container

teb.name: max_vel_x
teb.desc: Maximum translational velocity of the robot

teb.name: max_vel_x_backwards
teb.desc: Maximum translational velocity of the robot for driving backwards

teb.name: max_vel_theta
teb.desc: Maximum angular velocity of the robot

teb.name: acc_lim_x
teb.desc: Maximum translational acceleration of the robot

teb.name: acc_lim_theta
teb.desc: Maximum angular acceleration of the robot

teb.name: is_footprint_dynamic
teb.desc: If true, updated the footprint before checking trajectory feasibility

teb.name: xy_goal_tolerance
teb.desc: Allowed final euclidean distance to the goal position

teb.name: yaw_goal_tolerance
teb.desc: Allowed final orientation error to the goal orientation

teb.name: free_goal_vel
teb.desc: Allow the robot's velocity to be nonzero for planning purposes (the robot can arrive at the goal with max speed)

teb.name: min_obstacle_dist
teb.desc: Minimum desired separation from obstacles

teb.name: inflation_dist
teb.desc: Buffer zone around obstacles with non-zero penalty costs (should be larger than min_obstacle_dist in order to take effect)

teb.name: dynamic_obstacle_inflation_dist
teb.desc: Buffer zone around predicted locations of dynamic obstacles with non-zero penalty costs (should be larger than min_obstacle_dist in order to take effect)

teb.name: include_dynamic_obstacles
teb.desc: Specify whether the movement of dynamic obstacles should be predicted by a constant velocity model (this also changes the homotopy class search). If false, all obstacles are considered to be static.

teb.name: include_costmap_obstacles
teb.desc: Specify whether the obstacles in the costmap should be taken into account directly (this is necessary if no seperate clustering and detection is implemented)

teb.name: legacy_obstacle_association
teb.desc: If true, the old association strategy is used (for each obstacle, find the nearest TEB pose), otherwise the new one (for each teb pose, find only 'relevant' obstacles).

teb.name: obstacle_association_force_inclusion_factor
teb.desc: The non-legacy obstacle association technique tries to connect only relevant obstacles with the discretized trajectory during optimization, all obstacles within a specifed distance are forced to be included (as a multiple of min_obstacle_dist), e.g. choose 2.0 in order to consider obstacles within a radius of 2.0*min_obstacle_dist.

teb.name: obstacle_association_cutoff_factor
teb.desc: See obstacle_association_force_inclusion_factor, but beyond a multiple of [value]*min_obstacle_dist all obstacles are ignored during optimization. obstacle_association_force_inclusion_factor is processed first.

teb.name: costmap_obstacles_behind_robot_dist
teb.desc: Limit the occupied local costmap obstacles taken into account for planning behind the robot (specify distance in meters)

teb.name: obstacle_poses_affected
teb.desc: The obstacle position is attached to the closest pose on the trajectory to reduce computational effort, but take a number of neighbors into account as well

teb.name: no_inner_iterations
teb.desc: Number of solver iterations called in each outerloop iteration

teb.name: no_outer_iterations
teb.desc: Each outerloop iteration automatically resizes the trajectory and invokes the internal optimizer with no_inner_iterations

teb.name: optimization_activate
teb.desc: Activate the optimization

teb.name: optimization_verbose
teb.desc: Print verbose information

teb.name: penalty_epsilon
teb.desc: Add a small safty margin to penalty functions for hard-constraint approximations

teb.name: weight_max_vel_x
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed translational velocity

teb.name: weight_max_vel_y
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed strafing velocity (in use only for holonomic robots)

teb.name: weight_max_vel_theta
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed angular velocity

teb.name: weight_acc_lim_x
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed translational acceleration

teb.name: weight_acc_lim_y
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed strafing acceleration (in use only for holonomic robots)

teb.name: weight_acc_lim_theta
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the maximum allowed angular acceleration

teb.name: weight_kinematics_nh
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying the non-holonomic kinematics

teb.name: weight_kinematics_forward_drive
teb.desc: Optimization weight for forcing the robot to choose only forward directions (positive transl. velocities, only diffdrive robot)

teb.name: weight_kinematics_turning_radius
teb.desc: Optimization weight for enforcing a minimum turning radius (carlike robots)

teb.name: weight_optimaltime
teb.desc: Optimization weight for contracting the trajectory w.r.t. transition time

teb.name: weight_shortest_path
teb.desc: Optimization weight for contracting the trajectory w.r.t. path length

teb.name: weight_obstacle
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying a minimum seperation from obstacles

teb.name: weight_inflation
teb.desc: Optimization weight for the inflation penalty (should be small)

teb.name: weight_dynamic_obstacle
teb.desc: Optimization weight for satisfying a minimum seperation from dynamic obstacles

teb.name: weight_dynamic_obstacle_inflation
teb.desc: Optimization weight for the inflation penalty of dynamic obstacles (should be small)

teb.name: weight_viapoint
teb.desc: Optimization weight for minimizing the distance to via-points

teb.name: weight_adapt_factor
teb.desc: Some special weights (currently 'weight_obstacle') are repeatedly scaled by this factor in each outer TEB iteration (weight_new: weight_old * factor); Increasing weights iteratively instead of setting a huge value a-priori leads to better numerical conditions of the underlying optimization problem.

teb.name: obstacle_cost_exponent
teb.desc: Exponent for nonlinear obstacle cost (cost = linear_cost * obstacle_cost_exponent). Set to 1 to disable nonlinear cost (default)

teb.name: enable_multithreading
teb.desc: Activate multiple threading for planning multiple trajectories in parallel

teb.name: max_number_classes
teb.desc: Specify the maximum number of allowed alternative homotopy classes (limits computational effort)

teb.name: selection_cost_hysteresis
teb.desc: Specify how much trajectory cost must a new candidate have w.r.t. a previously selected trajectory in order to be selected (selection if new_cost < old_cost*factor)

teb.name: selection_prefer_initial_plan
teb.desc: Specify a cost reduction in the interval (0,1) for the trajectory in the equivalence class of the initial plan.)

teb.name: selection_obst_cost_scale
teb.desc: Extra scaling of obstacle cost terms just for selecting the 'best' candidate (new_obst_cost: obst_cost*factor)

teb.name: selection_viapoint_cost_scale
teb.desc: Extra scaling of via-point cost terms just for selecting the 'best' candidate. (new_viapt_cost: viapt_cost*factor)

teb.name: selection_alternative_time_cost
teb.desc: If true, time cost is replaced by the total transition time.

teb.name: switching_blocking_period
teb.desc: Specify a time duration in seconds that needs to be expired before a switch to new equivalence class is allowed

teb.name: roadmap_graph_no_samples
teb.desc: Specify the number of samples generated for creating the roadmap graph, if simple_exploration is turend off

teb.name: roadmap_graph_area_width
teb.desc: Specify the width of the area in which sampled will be generated between start and goal [m] (the height equals the start-goal distance)

teb.name: roadmap_graph_area_length_scale
teb.desc: The length of the rectangular region is determined by the distance between start and goal. This parameter further scales the distance such that the geometric center remains equal!)

teb.name: h_signature_prescaler
teb.desc: Scale number of obstacle value in order to allow huge number of obstacles. Do not choose it extremly low, otherwise obstacles cannot be distinguished from each other (0.2<H<=1)

teb.name: h_signature_threshold
teb.desc: Two h-signuteres are assumed to be equal, if both the difference of real parts and complex parts are below the specified threshold

teb.name: obstacle_heading_threshold
teb.desc: Specify the value of the normalized scalar product between obstacle heading and goal heading in order to take them (obstacles) into account for exploration)

teb.name: viapoints_all_candidates
teb.desc: If true, all trajectories of different topologies are attached to the set of via-points, otherwise only the trajectory sharing the same one as the initial/global plan is attached (no effect in test_optim_node).

teb.name: visualize_hc_graph
teb.desc: Visualize the graph that is created for exploring new homotopy classes

teb.name: shrink_horizon_backup
teb.desc: Allows the planner to shrink the horizon temporary (50%) in case of automatically detected issues.

teb.name: oscillation_recovery
teb.desc: Try to detect and resolve oscillations between multiple solutions in the same equivalence class (robot frequently switches between left/right/forward/backwards).

teb.name: max_vel_y
teb.desc: Maximum strafing velocity of the robot (should be zero for non-holonomic robots!)

teb.name: acc_lim_y
teb.desc: Maximum strafing acceleration of the robot

teb.name: min_turning_radius
teb.desc: Minimum turning radius of a carlike robot (diff-drive robot: zero)

teb.name: wheelbase
teb.desc: The distance between the drive shaft and steering axle (only required for a carlike robot with 'cmd_angle_instead_rotvel' enabled); The value might be negative for back-wheeled robots!

teb.name: cmd_angle_instead_rotvel
teb.desc: Substitute the rotational velocity in the commanded velocity message by the corresponding steering angle (check 'axles_distance')
